exact_statement: Fix n,s>=1. For every admissible noncommutative rational formula Phi over Q of tree size <=s, there is an exact black-box protocol using only n,s and at most one query per trial to an oracle Eval_Phi(X) that returns UNDEFINED on any original-tree inverse-domain failure, else the complete exact rational D-by-D value matrix. The protocol samples one parameter triple uniformly from {1,...,G'}^3, where G'=2^ceil(log2 G), G=1+3(s+2)B M^3, B=2s+1, Delta=2(n+1)^3 B, M is the least power of two >B Delta, D=M^2/2; it constructs X_i=Z_0^-1 Z_i when Z_0 is nonsingular and accepts exactly when Eval_Phi(X) is defined and invertible. For every operationally nonzero Phi, per-trial acceptance probability is >1/2; for every operationally zero Phi, acceptance probability is 0. After r independent trials, a nonzero Phi is accepted with probability >=1-2^-r. A trial uses 3 log2(G') random bits, candidate input length O((n+s+1)^36 log(n+s+1)), per-entry query-coordinate height O((n+s+1)^15 log(n+s+1)), D=O((n+s+1)^10), and can be implemented in O((n+s+1)^96 log^3(n+s+1)) bit operations with elementary arithmetic and a conservative Cramer-rule implementation. Formula oracle time and response length are additional charged costs and have no bound in n,s alone because rational leaf constants have no height bound.
assumptions: The formula is promised admissible in the operational sense of the pinned source.
The size bound s and variable count n are supplied in unary.
The evaluation oracle uses exact rational matrix semantics and respects every inverse occurrence in the original tree.

If the oracle returns matrix values, the protocol can test exact rational nonsingularity; a bit-only alternative must itself provide a correct defined-and-invertible predicate and its computation cost is charged.
The source's internal algebraic proof of the universal list construction is accepted; this report reconstructs rather than independently certifies that proof.
novelty_boundary: The success-probability claim is a direct Schwartz-Zippel corollary of the pinned paper's parameter-grid degree estimate, not a new universal hitting-list theorem. Existing randomized black-box rational identity testing is prior art; no priority claim is made. Companion single-point theorems cover division-free formulas only. Astra N51 is an unreviewed internal all-field integer-list candidate and not independent validation.

costs.random_bits: 3 log2(G')=O(log(n+s+1)) per trial, with G'=next power of two >= G
costs.query_input_bits: O((n+s+1)^36 log(n+s+1)) per attempted nonsingular-normalizer tuple
costs.coordinate_height_bits: O((n+s+1)^15 log(n+s+1)) per rational matrix entry encoding
costs.sampler_bit_time: O((n+s+1)^96 log^3(n+s+1)) per trial under classical integer arithmetic and the stated coarse Cramer implementation
costs.oracle_response: Exact full D-by-D rational matrix or UNDEFINED; actual response length L and oracle evaluation cost C_Phi(X) are charged separately; no bound in n,s alone
costs.precision: Exact only; no finite-precision robustness claim

falsifier: For a valid nonzero admissible formula, exhibit that the product determinant polynomial P_Phi used in §§3-5 can be identically zero or has degree >=G/2, or that some grid triple with P_Phi nonzero fails to give a defined invertible rational evaluation. A source-proof error in Proposition 3.2, Proposition 4.2, or Proposition 5.1 would also invalidate the corollary.
next_gate: Independently implement the one-triple constructor and test exact oracle acquisition on nested inverse formulas, dead inverse branches, high-height constants, and near-singular outputs; compare with existing randomized black-box RIT query/bit costs; determine whether the internal all-field N51 parameter construction has a constant-fraction sampler.
